diagnostic_evidence.quote: which is a consistent approximation \cite{NCpaper}, as the edge-lengths tend to zero.
The authors of \cite{NCpaper} approximate the inner product terms \cref{NCinnerprod} \textit{consistently}, in order to derive approximations for the normal cycles metric.

issues.failure_explanation: The formula NC_disc_met is obtained by collocating the spatial kernel at edge centres: the exact W*-inner product of the cylindrical currents contains integrals of K_p(x,y) over edge pairs, which are replaced by the midpoint values |e||e'|K_p(c,c'). For a non-constant spatial kernel (e.g. the Gaussian used throughout) this replacement is not an identity, so the equality asserted in Theorem thm:added-1 ('can be computed as') is false in general; the paper's own derivation writes the centre approximation with '\approx' and calls it only a consistent approximation, and the prose describes NC_disc_met as an approximation. The same slide from approximation to equality underlies the Dirac decomposition NC_delta, which asserts N(T) equals the delta sum 'as an element of W*'.

failure_location.quote: The inner product between the associated discrete Normal Cycles can be computed as,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State NC_disc_met and NC_delta as consistent approximations (replace the equalities by approximations with the quoted consistency as the mesh size tends to zero), or define the discrete normal-cycle metric by the formula; the compression algorithm, the bounds and the experiments then concern the approximating functional and are otherwise unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:added-1, and likewise the decomposition NC_delta and the embedding realembedding, overstate what is constructed: the discrete metric and the compressed object are consistent approximations of the normal cycle and its W*-metric, not exact realizations. Any exactness claim, and the transfer of the compression guarantee to the true normal cycle, additionally needs the cited consistency error terms.
issues.title: Discrete normal-cycle inner product stated as an exact computation although it is only a consistent approximation
issues.why_classification: The source itself supplies the approximation statement and its consistency, so the repair is a local correction of equality claims; every substantive method, rate and guarantee survives unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: one may check the resulting scalar product of $N(\mathcal{T}),N(\mathcal{T}') \in W^{*}$ of \cref{NC_delta} agrees with \cref{NC_disc_met} derived in \cite{NCpaper}.

issues.failure_explanation: The cylindrical derivation establishes N(T)^cyl = -(pi/2) sum_j delta_{c_j} gamma_j with gamma_j defined without a minus sign; absorbing the minus into the redefined gamma of NC_delta gives +(pi/2) sum delta gamma, but NC_delta writes pi sum delta gamma, twice the derived value, while realembedding keeps pi for the cylindrical part and changes the spherical part from pi (the value in NC_delta, and the one forced by the stated identity integral of u over a half-sphere = pi alpha) to pi/2, so the three displays are pairwise inconsistent. Using orthonormality of the wedge basis one computes <gamma_i,gamma'_j> = <f_i,g_j><sum_{T ni e_i} n_{T,e_i}, sum_{T' ni e'_j} n_{T',e'_j}> and <alpha_i,alpha'_j> = <A_i,B_j>, hence the scalar product of the NC_delta functionals equals pi^2 times each part, i.e. exactly 4 times the corresponding terms of NC_disc_met, whose prefactor is pi^2/4 on both parts; the asserted agreement of NC_delta with NC_disc_met is therefore false as written, and none of the three displays reproduces NC_disc_met on both terms. The curve delta form N(C) = sum delta_{x_i} A_i likewise omits the pi/2 per-vertex factor needed to yield the pi^2/4 prefactor of Theorem thm:added-2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Fix the constants consistently: the derivation forces the cylindrical prefactor pi/2 (which also restores agreement of the edge term with NC_disc_met); reconcile the spherical prefactor (pi from the derivation, pi/2 required by NC_disc_met) by correcting either the boundary decomposition or the quoted boundary term; propagate the corrected constants to NC_delta, realembedding and the curve delta form, and correct the agreement claim.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central construction is quantitatively wrong as written: the functional embedded into V* and fed to the compression algorithm (alg:added-1) and to the guarantee (thm:added-3) is a component-wise constant rescaling of the discrete normal cycle (cylindrical part doubled, spherical part halved in realembedding relative to the derivation), not the functional whose metric is NC_disc_met. The claimed identification with the discrete normal-cycle metric of [NCpaper] fails by factors of 4 in the inner products; for surfaces with boundary this changes the relative weighting of edge and boundary contributions in the metric used in Section numexp, while for closed surfaces it is a global rescaling of the functional.
issues.title: Wrong and mutually inconsistent normalization constants in the Dirac delta decomposition
issues.why_classification: The construction, the algorithm, the rates and the (closed-surface) experiments all survive a correction of constants, so there is no major loss; but the repair requires a nontrivial consistency pass over several displays and a false agreement claim, and the source itself offers conflicting values for the spherical constant (derivation versus quoted theorem), so the correction is not a single forced edit.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: is a positively oriented orthonomal basis of $\R^{3}$.  In particular, note that at a given point $(x,u)$ on the cylindrical component, such a basis may be computed as

issues.failure_explanation: On cylindrical components u is orthogonal to f, so f/|f| x (f/|f| x u) = -u; hence e1 x e2 = -u and the displayed frame is negatively oriented, contradicting the stated requirement of a positively oriented orthonormal basis (the same requirement that on spherical pieces is used to identify the coefficients of tau with u via u = e1 x e2). With the paper's stated convention the computed tau, the integral alpha, and therefore the cylindrical weights gamma_j carry the opposite sign. Separately, the spherical reduction asserts N(T)^sph = -pi sum delta_{x_k} alpha_k although every displayed ingredient is positive (the currents in boundarysph appear with + signs and the integral of u over a half-sphere is +pi alpha), so the substitution as written yields +pi sum delta_{x_k} alpha_k; the overall minus sign is unsupported within the source. The signs of the delta weights in NC_delta are therefore not established by the derivation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the positively oriented frame (f/|f|, u x f/|f|, u) (or explicitly adopt the opposite orientation convention), and either justify the spherical minus sign from the orientation of the boundary currents or remove it, propagating any resulting sign changes to gamma_j and alpha_i.
issues.overall_effect: The Dirac weights of NC_delta/realembedding may represent sign-flipped cylindrical and spherical components relative to the oriented normal cycle. Because the K_s = 1 metric is quadratic in each component and the components are mutually orthogonal in W*, these sign errors cancel out of every inner product, so the metric formulas, the compression algorithm and the experiments are unaffected; the defect concerns the correctness of the functional identity itself.
issues.title: Cylindrical frame declared positively oriented is negatively oriented; unsupported minus sign in the spherical component
issues.why_classification: Local sign/convention corrections with no effect on any metric, rate or experimental claim; all substantive results survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem's conclusion bounds the squared norm of the difference between the compressed functional and sum_i delta_{x_i} alpha-hat_i, but alpha-hat_i is never defined anywhere in the paper; the object the approximation is meant to approximate is the stated target mu_S = sum_i delta_{x_i} alpha_i. As written the guarantee is therefore not a statement about the compression error ||mu_S - mu-hat||_{V*}. Even under the forced reading alpha-hat = alpha, the bound cannot hold with a constant C independent of the weights: for the orthogonal-projection weights beta = K_{CC}^{-1} Y_c one has ||mu_S - mu-hat||^2_{V*} = tr(A^T (K_{XX} - Q_{XX}) A) with A = (alpha_1,...,alpha_n)^T, which scales quadratically in A while tr(K_{XX} - Q_{XX}) is independent of A, so rescaling A to tA violates any weight-independent bound for large t. The same undefined alpha-hat and the same missing weight dependence recur in the eigenvalue bound eigenbound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the guarantees with the true target on the left-hand side, e.g. ||mu_S - sum_j delta_{c_j} beta_j||^2_{V*} = tr(A^T (K_{XX} - Q_{XX}) A) <= ||A||_F^2 tr(K_{XX} - Q_{XX}), and eigenbound as C ||A||_F^2 (n/S) sum_{i>S} lambda_i(K_{XX}); for the fixed target functional this preserves the advertised exponential-in-m decay.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's only stated convergence guarantee (Theorem thm:added-3, displays tracebound and eigenbound) is ill-formed as written. The subsequent prose claim that the randomized compression error decays like the eigenvalue tail (exponentially in m for Gaussian kernels) and the numerical comparison against the trace bound in Section numexp rely on the intended standard statement rather than the displayed one.
issues.title: Compression guarantee bounds distance to an undefined functional and omits the weight-dependent constant
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local, standard restatement (the projection identity plus a trace inequality, with the constant allowed to depend on the fixed weights); the method, the advertised exponential rate and the scope all survive, and no new lemma, construction or replacement argument is required.
